calls.head: The matchup inside the matchup
calls.body: The Flames are one of the league’s best for shot volume, and the Avalanche are near the top of the league at keeping shots away. We think the Flames still get theirs.
calls.call: The Flames take more than the league-average 56.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 against the Avalanche.
calls.nums: Calgary 4th for shot volume (64.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Colorado 8th for keeping shots away
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts, Calgary had 58.9 per 60. The league average is 56.3 per 60, and they came in at 64.2 per 60.

calls.head: Don’t count on Blackwood to stand on his head again
calls.body: Blackwood has been a wall against the Flames since 2023-24, well above his usual. It looks like a pattern, but across three seasons a goalie’s record against one team told us nothing about the next meeting. Expect the usual Blackwood.
calls.call: If Blackwood starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .907 than to his .939 against the Flames.
calls.nums: 5 starts against Calgary: .939 save percentage · .907 against everyone else
calls.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 5 against Calgary, 3,684 shots against everyone else
calls.happened: He didn’t start, so this call can’t be judged.

calls.head: The Avalanche feed on mistakes, and the Flames make them
calls.body: The Flames give up more dangerous chances after losing the puck than most, and the Avalanche pounce.
calls.call: The Avalanche get at least their usual 7.7% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
calls.nums: Colorado 4th for chances off turnovers (7.7% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · Calgary 30th for avoiding breakdowns
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: 3.3% of Colorado’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against their usual 7.7%.

calls.head: Expect a track meet
calls.body: Colorado plays some of the league’s fastest games, and so does Calgary. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at more than 88.6 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, faster than either team’s usual.
calls.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): Colorado 1st (88.6), Calgary 3rd (85.3)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 97.4 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the faster team’s usual 88.6 and a league average of 82.0.

CGY.head: We gave Calgary only a 28% chance, and it went the way we feared.

COL.head: We gave Colorado a 72% chance, and Colorado delivered.

surprises.head: A rough night for D. Cooley
surprises.body: D. Cooley allowed 7 goals on shots worth 2.8 expected goals, 4.2 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 200 starts over the last three seasons.

surprises.head: Colorado leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: Colorado’s bottom-six forwards played 46% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 39% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 175 games.

story.head: The Avalanche roll past the Flames
paras: Devon Toews scored twice, opening the scoring late in the first. Cale Makar and Jaden Schwartz added two each. Four different Avalanche scored.
The chances were closer than the score. By our Swing measure, Mikael Backlund had the best night of anyone, even in a loss.

items.text: The Flames haven’t won in four.
Nicolas Roy faces his old team, Toronto, on Saturday.
Two of the preview’s three calls held.
